questions.q: In mission-tile roofing, what is the usual role of the convex-up unit?
o: It acts as the cap covering the joint between adjacent pan units
questions.n: The cap tile bridges the joint between concave-up pan tiles.

questions.q: How does a drained basement system principally manage water?
o: It eliminates hydrostatic pressure by removing the wall
It uses roof shingles below grade
It provides a controlled drainage path so water is collected and removed
questions.n: Drained systems manage ingress by channeling water to drainage and sump/discharge systems.

questions.q: Why can tightly stacked wet galvanized sheets be vulnerable to white rust?
o: The sheets are heated above melting point
Trapped moisture and restricted air circulation promote zinc corrosion products
The sheets lose all zinc immediately
questions.n: Persistent moisture without drying promotes white rust.

questions.q: A precast panel has two concrete wythes separated by rigid insulation. What assembly type is this?
questions.n: Two facings with a thicker insulation core form a sandwich panel.

o: Temporary formwork/support for an arch, dome, or vault
questions.ref: Francis D.K. Ching / Cyril M. Harris
questions.n: Centering carries masonry or concrete arch/vault work until it can support itself.

questions.q: Which strategy is generally positioned on the positive water-pressure side of a basement wall?
questions.n: External membranes are located on the side from which groundwater pressure acts.

o: A waterproof barrier applied to the interior side of a below-grade enclosure
questions.n: Internal tanking provides a continuous waterproof treatment on the inside face of the basement enclosure.

o: A white zinc-corrosion product that can form on galvanized steel under wet, poorly ventilated conditions
Red iron oxide on bare steel
questions.ref: Galvanizers Association / ASTM galvanized-steel corrosion guidance
questions.n: White rust is associated with corrosion products of the zinc coating on galvanized steel.

questions.q: What is the main risk of relying on an internal barrier where groundwater pressure acts from outside?
o: Water pressure still reaches the wall and can challenge adhesion or cause leakage paths
questions.n: Negative-side systems are exposed to hydrostatic pressure acting through the substrate.

questions.q: What is a canton in traditional architectural terminology?
o: A projecting corner column or corner feature
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction
questions.n: Canton is used for a projecting architectural element at a building corner.

questions.q: Why does a sandwich panel gain bending stiffness efficiently?
o: The two facings are separated by a thicker core, increasing structural depth
questions.n: Separating strong facings increases section depth and bending efficiency.

o: A continuous waterproof barrier applied on the outside, water-facing side of the basement enclosure
questions.n: External tanking resists water before it enters the basement wall/floor assembly.

questions.q: In an insulated precast concrete sandwich panel, what commonly occupies the middle layer?
o: A nonstructural or semi-structural insulation core
questions.n: Precast sandwich panels commonly place insulation between two concrete wythes.

questions.q: When may arch centering be removed?
o: Only after the building is demolished
After the arch or vault has developed sufficient self-supporting capacity
questions.n: Centering remains until the arch system can safely carry itself.

questions.q: Which traditional roof tile uses semi-cylindrical units laid in alternating convex-up and convex-down courses?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction
questions.n: Mission tile roofing uses alternating cap and pan semicylindrical units.

questions.q: Which conventional building method is often considered simplest for small low-rise construction because of repetitive light members and straightforward connections?
questions.ref: Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated
questions.n: Wood light framing uses repetitive standardized members and simple fastening methods.

questions.q: Which item is a structural function rather than a water-control strategy for basement wall construction?
questions.n: Drained and tanked approaches describe water-control strategies; retaining describes the wall's structural role.

o: A layered panel with two relatively thin facings bonded or connected to a thicker core
questions.n: Sandwich panels use separated faces and a core to combine stiffness, enclosure, and insulation functions.
